newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank plans Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank plans Eurobond.

text.p: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank (NRB) plans to get a credit rating for a Eurobond issue next year, the bank's chairman said.
But Alexander Lebedev said the bank was not yet well enough known to do consider an issue immediately.
"We shall not raise the issue of depositary receipts or Eurobonds seriously earlier than in three or five months," he told a news conference late on Wednesday.

NRB has grown sharply over the last year to become one of Russia's biggest banks. It specialises in trading Russian foreign debt and has the second-biggest portfolio of government securities after Sberegatelny Bank RF, Russia's biggest bank.
It has already announced plans to issue Global Depositary Receipts representing Ukrainian debt to Russia's natural gas monopoly RAO Gazprom.
Before issuing the Eurobond the bank must be converted from a mutual into a joint-stock bank, Lebedev said.
"We shall announce our plans to turn into a joint-stock bank sometime in February," he said. "We must finish the process of forming our authorised capital."
Lebedev said the proportion of shareholdings in the bank would not change after the process was over.
In October a shareholders' meeting decided to convert the bank into a joint-stock company and to raise its capital to five trillion roubles from one trillion roubles.
Gazprom and its export unit VEP Gazprom are among the bank's biggest shareholders.
